strings.d1.s0.name: Aya Yorgi Church
strings.d1.s0.tips: Take the 09:00 ferry from Kabataş, then ride an electric minibus from the pier or walk the 40-minute uphill path to Yücetepe. At the top you'll find the church and views over the Marmara.
strings.d1.s1.name: Yücetepe Kır Gazinosu
strings.d1.s1.tips: Köfte (grilled meatballs) and gözleme (stuffed flatbread) with a view, just below Aya Yorgi.
strings.d1.s2.name: Nakibey Beach
strings.d1.s2.tips: Closed in winter; walk the coastal road instead.
strings.d1.s3.name: Lunapark Square
strings.d1.s3.tips: A pine-shaded square in the middle of the island and the starting point for bike tours.
strings.d1.s4.name: Ali Baba Restaurant Büyükada
strings.d1.s4.tips: A long-established fish restaurant by the pier, serving meze and fish. In winter the enclosed section is heated.
strings.d1.b0.name: Milto Restaurant Büyükada
strings.d1.b1.name: Eskibağ Beach
strings.d1.b1.tips: A pine-shaded beach on the west of the island, an alternative to Nakibey.
strings.d2.s0.name: Büyükada Bike Rental
strings.d2.s0.tips: Rent a bike behind the pier (about 300 TL/day); the big loop is 12 km.
strings.d2.s1.name: Büyükada Grand Tour Road
strings.d2.s1.tips: A paved road around the island, with pine forest and coves.
strings.d2.s2.name: Dil Burnu
strings.d2.s2.tips: A nature park for winter walks and views.
strings.d2.s3.name: Kalpazankaya Restaurant Büyükada
strings.d2.s3.tips: Fish and meze by the sea at Kalpazankaya; the sunset here is famous.
strings.d2.s4.name: Çankaya Avenue Mansions
strings.d2.s4.tips: Greek mansions and the John Pasha Mansion: wooden architecture.
strings.d2.b0.name: Kalpazankaya Beach
strings.d2.b0.tips: A rocky beach, an alternative to Dil Burnu.
strings.d2.b1.name: Lokmacı Square Büyükada
strings.d2.b1.tips: Hot lokma (syrup-soaked dough fritters) in the square.
strings.d3.s0.name: Halki Seminary
strings.d3.s0.tips: A Greek Orthodox school founded on the hilltop in 1844. Enjoy the garden and views; visits are guided.
strings.d3.s1.name: Çam Limanı
strings.d3.s1.tips: A winter walk with views over the bay.
strings.d3.s2.name: Heybeliada Meydan Balıkçısı
strings.d3.s3.name: Naval High School Shore
strings.d3.s3.tips: The coastal road and Aya Triada; take the ferry back.
strings.d3.b0.name: Heybeliada Lokantası
strings.d3.b1.name: Değirmen Tepesi
strings.d4.s0.name: Sait Faik Museum
strings.d4.s0.tips: The writer's house, and the literary heart of the island.
strings.d4.s1.name: Kalpazankaya Burgazada
strings.d4.s2.name: Kalpazankaya Restaurant Burgazada
strings.d4.s2.tips: Fish and meze on the cove.
strings.d4.s3.name: Kınalıada Beach
strings.d4.s3.tips: The smallest island, with red earth and a seaside walk; you change ferries here.
strings.d4.b0.name: Burgazada Meydan Kahvaltıcısı
strings.d4.b1.name: Aya Yani Church
strings.d4.b1.tips: The church on the square, an alternative to the cove.
strings.d5.s0.name: Princes' Islands Museum
strings.d5.s0.tips: The history of the islands at Aya Nikola, including their Greek, Armenian and Jewish heritage.
strings.d5.s1.name: Hamidiye Mosque
strings.d5.s1.tips: The mosque of Abdulhamid II, near the pier.
strings.d5.s2.name: Prinkipo Greek Orphanage
strings.d5.s2.tips: The largest wooden building in Europe (seen from outside); walk through the forest.
strings.d5.s3.name: Prinkipo Breakfast
strings.d5.s4.name: Phaeton Square
strings.d5.s4.tips: The old phaeton (horse carriage) square, now with an electric vehicle stop and coffee.
strings.d5.b0.name: Ice Cream Shop on the Square
strings.d5.b0.tips: Island ice cream; a light lunch.
strings.d5.b1.name: Aya Dimitri Church
strings.d5.b1.tips: A Greek church, an alternative to the mosque.
strings.d6.s0.name: Sedef Island
strings.d6.s0.tips: Boats are infrequent in winter; do the Dil Burnu walk on Büyükada instead.
strings.d6.s1.name: Sedef Island Beach Restaurant
strings.d6.s2.name: Aya Nikola Shore
strings.d6.s2.tips: The island's east coast, with rocks and a spot to be before sunset.
strings.d6.b0.name: By Şükrü Restaurant Büyükada
strings.d6.b0.tips: A fish restaurant on Gülistan Avenue.
strings.d6.b1.name: Public Beach Büyükada
strings.d6.b1.tips: A free beach, an alternative to Sedef.
strings.d7.s0.name: Büyükada Pier Square
strings.d7.s0.tips: The clock tower and square, quiet in the morning.
strings.d7.s1.name: Pastry Shop Büyükada
strings.d7.s1.tips: An island pastry shop for breakfast and ice cream.
strings.d7.s2.name: Plane Tree Square Büyükada
strings.d7.s2.tips: A last stroll, then take the 12:30 ferry back to Kabataş.
strings.d7.b0.name: Pier Tea Garden Büyükada
strings.d7.b0.tips: Tea and simit (sesame bread ring) at the pier: a farewell.
strings.d7.b1.name: Gülistan Avenue
strings.d7.b1.tips: A street of fish restaurants by the shore.
strings.note0: Ferries (Istanbulkart) leave from Kabataş and Bostancı every 30 minutes in summer and hourly in winter; the last ferry is around 20:00.
strings.note1: There are no cars on the island: use an electric minibus, a bike or your feet. The Aya Yorgi climb takes 40 minutes; an electric vehicle costs 100 TL.
strings.note2: The islands are quiet in winter: the fish restaurants on Gülistan Avenue are heated and the beaches are closed. Istanbul residents come at weekends.
strings.note3: Try hot lokma, island ice cream and fish with meze; the restaurants on Gülistan Avenue don't need reservations.
strings.note4: ATMs are scarce on the islands, so bring cash.
strings.note5: Ferries between the islands take 15 minutes.
